newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: TENNIS - SICKLY EDBERG EDGES OUT TOP SEED MUSTER.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS - SICKLY EDBERG EDGES OUT TOP SEED MUSTER.

text.p: A sickly Stefan Edberg moved a step closer to capturing one more title before his retirement when he beat top seed Thomas Muster in the CA Trophy on Thursday.
The Swede, who plans to quit the game at the end of the year, edged out the Austrian world number three 6-4 6-7 7-5.
Edberg, still recovering from a bout of flu which forced him to pull out of last week's tournament in Lyon, stretched his run of victories over claycourt specialist Muster to nine.
Muster dropped his serve in the opening game to lose the first set but levelled the match by winning he second set tiebreak 7-2.
In the final set of a suberb match, Edberg profited from Muster's first double fault of the match to seal victory in a little over two hours.
French Open champion Yevgeny Kafelnikov continued his pursuit of his fifth title of the year with an emphatic 6-4 6-3 win over Italian qualifier Omar Camporese.
Kafelnikov had a slow start against Camporese, dropping serve in the seventh game, before stepping up a gear for two consecutive breaks to claim the set.
He clinched the match with a second-set break at 5-3 in a little over an hour.
Fifth seeded Boris Becker required three sets to knock out fellow German Michael Stich 3-6 6-3 6-4 to increase his lead in the head-to-head between the pair 8-4.
Becker had a slow start, dropping serve in the sixth game to lose the first set, before regaining his form and taking the second set with a thundering ace.
In the decisive set, Becker's form wavered slightly and he dropped serve at 3-4 when he was forced to change rackets just after breaking Stich's serve.
But the three-time Wimbledon champion broke back immediately to clinch the match on serve a game later.
